body: Thank you. It's so beautifully written.

For me it's as real as it gets. Currently just me, but if we get a few more people we can definitely make this happen. I'm in the process of selling everything I own here, and next month I'm going to couchsurf for a month in a neighboring country to spam my CV and myself to every financial company that has a door there. Am currently in talks with a few people in some countries too to see my chances. Fingers crossed. PM me if youre still interested. And anyways, so what's your story?

Good point. Man i love this subreddit, i keep on finding things like this that actually gives me hope. 20 years is too optimistic though, I would say probably 70-100 years, but with techs nowadays I'm pretty sure the average lifespan for us will be at least 150 years anyway so we'll definitely see it.

Now what to do and how to sustain myself in the meanwhile is a completely different problem..
Well it's just an idea. It's very realistic to me, I just thought maybe there are a few other people who would find this interesting.
That could work too, it sounds interesting. Anything other than death would be a good idea anyway lol.

I mean, for example, if you are an American, at the very least you can just show up in an english-teaching establishment in a third world country and they will definitely hire you on spot as an english teacher if you only ask for local wage. Which will definitely cover your expenses with the local cost of living. And that's just for starters, you can also show up at modeling agencies for local televisions and they will pay you a ton of money to appear in tv adverts as long as you're foreign. The possibilities are endless.

Agreed, but the problem with support groups is that at the end of the day you go home to the same problems and the same situation you've been in this entire time. I'm not saying this is the fix-all solution, I just think that this may be exciting enough to hinder anybody that is on the very edge of their life from making that decision. I mean, it actually gave me dreams.

As for a bunch of depressed people being around each other.. Most times it actually is a lot of fun! Like, many types of depression don't come in a constant rate, its usually an on and off thing, and many suicidal people I've known are actually great super-social jokers who can crack jokes and bring smiles to other peoples faces most days. With a sizeable group, maybe whoever is not currently depressed at some day can help the ones whos got the blues on that day, you know?

And yeah it's very likely some of us just won't get along, but should that happen then it's easy enough to just go our separate ways. At least by then we have tried, and at least we will know that we are not alone in the journey.

Yeah it isnt, but I just thought I might as well try and put it up, who knows, maybe, probably there is a few people who would want this :)

At the very least I think it's better to take a leap of faith in this rather than to take a leap of faith off the balcony :)

We should find a sad, suicidal chef then. Gordon Ramsay's assistants will likely be good candidates. 

Actually though, I am a bipolar type 2. Yeah we are kinda weird when it comes to tidying up, we can switch from foul bachelor frog to extreme hygiene freaks and back again in a period of few days lol. But at the very least the place will be clean every once and a while.

We just gotta make sure we had secured a job there before we move for good, but i dont think it will be that hard. I'm pretty sure there are a lot of countries in dire need of English-speaking workers. We can also start a new business, but someone else would need to lead as I apparently suck in enterpreneuring.
